title: Cookies vs localStorage vs sessionStorage
intro: Three ways to store data in the browser, each built for a different job.

slides.heading: Cookies
slides.subtitle: Small data sent with requests.
points: Can be httpOnly so JavaScript can't read them

slides.heading: localStorage
slides.subtitle: Browser storage that persists.
points: Around 5MB per site in most browsers
Readable by any script on the page

slides.heading: Security tip
slides.subtitle: Choose storage carefully.
points: Never store passwords in the browser
Prefer httpOnly cookies for auth tokens

scenario.situation: An app stores the user's login token in localStorage.
scenario.problem: An XSS bug lets an injected script read localStorage and send the token to an attacker.
scenario.fix: Keep the session in an httpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookie. JavaScript can't read it, so XSS can't steal it.
scenario.takeaway: Keep auth tokens out of JavaScript's reach.

cta: Where do you store auth tokens in your apps?
